questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

My parents have promised that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.

options.text: I have been promised by my parents that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.
I am promised by my parents that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.
I am being promised by my parents that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.
I have promised by my parents that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****I have been promised by my parents that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **active voice.** As per the question we have to change it into** passive voice.**
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + have + past tense + Object (Active voice) + adjunct
 
• **Subject (objective case) + have been + past participle + Object (subjective case) (Passive voice) + adjunct**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *I have taken him out. (Active voice)*
 
• *He has been taken out by me. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘my parents’.
 
• The object of the given subject is ‘I’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **have promised** will be changed to **have been promised**.
 
• **Adjunct **is a word or phrase that constitutes an optional element or is considered of secondary importance in a sentence
 
 
• In the given sentence, *if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US *is the **adjunct. **
 
 

Correct sentence - I have been promised by my parents that if I do well in my school exams, they’ll send me to the US.

__

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Mother said, “You must stay indoors to remain safe.”

options.text: Mother told me that I have to stay indoors to remain safe.
Mother told me that I should stay indoors to remain safe.
Mother told me that I would stay indoors to remain safe.
Mother told me that I would have to stay indoors to remain safe.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****Mother told me that I should stay indoors to remain safe.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **assertive sentence.**
 
• While** changing the narration of an assertive sentence,** we need to follow steps - 
 
 
• The **reporting verb said** changes to '**told'. **( This is because we use told when we normally say who is spoken to which in this case is **me.** In other assertive sentences which does not have a direct personal object, the reporting verb said remains unchanged.)
 
• The **conjunction 'that'** is used in place of commas and inverted commas. 
 
• The **second person 'you' **in the direct speech should be changed to the **third person ****me.**
 
• The **modal verb 'must'** changes to **should.**
 
 
 
• Eventually, we will get the final sentence- **"Mother told me that I should stay indoors to remain safe.​"**

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. I stood upon the hearth-rug and picked up the stick which our visitor had left behind him the night before.

B. Moreover, it was just such a stick as Mortimer, the old-fashioned family lawyer used to carry - dignified, solid, and reassuring.

C. It was a fine, thick piece of wood, bulbous-headed, of the sort which is known as a “Penang lawyer.”

D. “Tell me, Watson, what do you make of our visitor’s stick?” I asked after he had examined it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'A, C, B, D'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual__ connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. **

__
 
• Sentence **A **is the independent sentence and sets the tone of the passage.
 
• So, sentence **A **is the **first **sentence after rearrangement. It talks about how the subject (I) picked up a stick left behind by a visitor. 
 
• Sentence **C **describes the stick. Hence, **C follows A.__**
 
• Sentence **B **which further describes the stick's appearance and uses the conjunction moreover should come after sentence** C**, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence **D** is the concluding statement of the passage as it talks about someone asking the subject about the stick.

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is **option 4 i.e. **A, C, B, D**.**

**So, the correct paragraph is : (*A) I stood upon the hearth-rug and picked up the stick which our visitor had left behind him the night before. (C) It was a fine, thick piece of wood, bulbous-headed, of the sort which is known as a “Penang lawyer.” (B) Moreover, it was just such a stick as Mortimer, the old-fashioned family lawyer used to carry - dignified, solid, and reassuring. (D) “Tell me, Watson, what do you make of our visitor’s stick?” I asked after he had examined it. ***

questions.question:

The nurse helped the patient to stand up.

options.text: The patient was helped by the nurse to stand up.
The patient was helping by the nurse to stand up.
The patient had been helped by the nurse to stand up.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'****The patient was helped by the nurse to stand up.**'

• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• **Subject + past participle + Object (Active voice)**
 
• **Subject (objective case) + was + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)**
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *She built a large garden. (Active voice)*
 
• *A large garden was built by her. (Passive voice)*
 
 
 
• The **subject **of the given sentence is ‘the nurse’.
 
• The **object **of the given subject is ‘the patient’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **helped **will be changed to **was helped**.
 
• Correct sentence - The patient was helped by the nurse to stand up.
